correctness.rationale: For 429 exactly enumerated ASMs, the full joint-cylinder Gram entry is the integer sum of binomial coefficients of the pairwise agreement count. Exact elimination gives degree-three rank 425 over F_101; four explicit independent integer null vectors establish the reverse inequality over R by direct G_3 annihilation. Degree-four Gram has rank 429 over F_101. Independent monotone-triangle enumeration and F_1009 elimination reproduce both ranks. The kernel vectors each sum to zero; two have eight positive and eight negative entries, giving distinct equal-marginal probability distributions. Character-cylindrical span equivalence is a tensor-product change of basis.

originality.rationale: The new claim is exact cubic Fourier sampling rank and its complete signed-measure kernel for 429 labelled order-five ASMs, not a counting formula or pointwise evaluation of a few correlations. Behrend (2012) addresses bulk/boundary refinements, prescribed multiple rows and columns, not the rank of all three-cell cylinders over arbitrary measures; Colomo–Pronko (2005) treats boundary two-point correlations; Brualdi et al. (2011) treats patterns, term rank and signed-graph structure. Index searches and the accessible historical claim comparisons gave no result implying 425/429 or a four-vector kernel. Unindexed equivalent work remains a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: No exhaustive mathematical census of every unpublished or unindexed ASM rank table was possible.
Some general six-vertex correlation identities might implicitly evaluate the same matrix without stating the rank; no implication was established from inspected sections.
The complete older relevant pattern paper was not exhaustively read; its primary introductory claims are on distinct invariants.

value.rationale: This determines a natural, exact finite cutoff for distribution recovery in the classical 429-state order-five ASM/six-vertex system: all cubic marginals miss precisely four directions, while all quartic marginals suffice. The complete four-dimensional signed-measure kernel, including two explicit 16-state ambiguities, provides structural information for an inverse problem not supplied by enumeration alone. Finite scope and absence of a general order-n theorem are explicit and do not negate the motivated exact invariant.
